channel.title: Nick Gustafson
channel.description: Holding the LLM Stack in Your Head — a dependency-ordered walk through the full LLM stack, from linear algebra to agent protocols. A living document, continuously revised.

item.title: Holding the LLM Stack in Your Head
item.description: A personal journey through the full LLM stack — how I built the mental models, how the series actually gets written, and where to jump in.

item.title: Vectors, Matrices, and the Spaces They Live In
item.description: Vectors as lists of activations, matrix multiplication as a linear map, and why every neural network operation bottoms out in matmuls.

item.title: Norms, Dot Products, and Similarity
item.description: How cosine similarity, L2 distance, and projections work, and why they show up everywhere from attention scores to embedding retrieval.

item.title: Distributions, Softmax, and the Chain Rule of Words
item.description: Softmax, categorical distributions, Bayes' rule, and the chain rule of probability — the four tools that make language modeling a well-defined math problem.

item.title: Cross-Entropy, KL Divergence, and What Loss Functions Measure
item.description: Why cross-entropy is the standard LM loss, what it actually measures about two distributions, and how it connects to perplexity.

item.title: Gradients and How Machines Learn
item.description: What a gradient is, why it points uphill, how backpropagation computes one efficiently via the chain rule, and what SGD does with it.

item.title: Optimizers: Momentum, Adam, and Learning Rate Schedules
item.description: Why vanilla SGD is too slow, how Adam adapts per-parameter, and how warmup and cosine decay shape training dynamics.

item.title: GPUs, Floating Point, and Why Precision Matters
item.description: IEEE 754, the difference between fp32/fp16/bfloat16, why mixed-precision training works, and the basics of GPU parallelism.

item.title: A Short Prehistory of Statistical NLP
item.description: The arc from rule-based systems through statistical MT and log-linear models to neural approaches, giving you historical context for everything that follows.

item.title: Language Modeling as Next-Token Prediction
item.description: Why 'predict the next word' is a surprisingly powerful training objective, and how it connects to the chain rule of probability.

item.title: N-gram Models and the Curse of Sparsity
item.description: Counting-based language models, Markov assumptions, smoothing techniques, and why sparsity made n-grams hit a hard ceiling.

item.title: Word2vec and the Embedding Revolution
item.description: How skip-gram and CBOW learn dense word vectors, why 'king - man + woman = queen' works, and what distributional semantics actually means.

item.title: GloVe, FastText, and the Embedding Zoo
item.description: How GloVe combines count-based and predictive methods, how FastText handles subwords, and the trade-offs across embedding approaches.

item.title: Recurrent Neural Networks and Sequence Modeling
item.description: The RNN equations, how hidden states carry information forward, why vanilla RNNs suffer from vanishing gradients, and what that means in practice.

item.title: LSTMs, GRUs, and Gated Memory
item.description: How gates solve the vanishing gradient problem, the difference between LSTM and GRU cells, and why gated architectures dominated NLP for five years.

item.title: Seq2seq, Bahdanau Attention, and Why Recurrence Hit a Wall
item.description: Encoder-decoder architectures, how additive attention let models align source and target tokens, and why sequential processing fundamentally bottlenecked scale.

item.title: Unicode, Bytes, and What Text Actually Is
item.description: UTF-8 encoding, code points vs. grapheme clusters, and why 'one character' is a surprisingly ambiguous concept for a model.

item.title: Byte-Pair Encoding from Scratch
item.description: The BPE merge algorithm step by step, implemented from scratch, showing how a raw byte stream becomes a vocabulary.

item.title: WordPiece, Unigram, and SentencePiece
item.description: How WordPiece (BERT) and Unigram (T5) differ from BPE, why SentencePiece operates on raw text, and when each approach wins.

item.title: Vocabulary Size, Merge Order, and Fertility
item.description: How vocabulary size affects model capacity and sequence length, what token fertility measures, and the practical trade-offs behind 32k vs. 128k vs. 200k vocabularies.

item.title: The Embedding Table and Its Geometry
item.description: How token IDs become vectors via a lookup table, why the embedding matrix is a learned linear map, and how embedding and unembedding layers relate.

item.title: Special Tokens, Chat Templates, and Input Formatting
item.description: BOS/EOS/PAD tokens, how chat-template formatting encodes multi-turn structure, system prompts, and tool-call schemas into a flat token stream.

item.title: Packing, Masking, and Tokenization as a Model Interface
item.description: Sequence packing for training efficiency, how attention masks prevent cross-contamination, and why tokenizer choices constrain everything downstream.

item.title: Self-Attention: Q, K, V from First Principles
item.description: Queries, keys, and values as learned linear projections, how scaled dot-product computes soft token-to-token lookups, and exactly why we divide by sqrt(d_k).

item.title: Multi-Head Attention and Representation Subspaces
item.description: Why multiple attention heads let the model attend to different relationship types in parallel, how heads partition the embedding dimension, and what the output projection does.

item.title: Causal Masking and the Autoregressive Constraint
item.description: Why decoder models must not attend to future tokens, how the triangular mask enforces this, and how masking shapes both training and generation.

item.title: Positional Encodings: Sinusoidal, Learned, RoPE, and ALiBi
item.description: Why attention is position-agnostic by default, how each encoding scheme injects order, why RoPE became dominant, and how ALiBi achieves length extrapolation.

item.title: The Feed-Forward Block as Key-Value Memory
item.description: The two-layer MLP that follows attention, why it can be interpreted as a learned key-value store over concepts, and what the intermediate dimension controls.

item.title: Layer Normalization: Pre-Norm, Post-Norm, and RMSNorm
item.description: Why normalization is essential for deep residual networks, how pre-norm stabilizes training, and why RMSNorm replaced LayerNorm in modern architectures.

item.title: Decoder-Only vs. Encoder-Decoder: Architecture Trade-offs
item.description: The structural differences between GPT-style and T5-style models, why decoder-only won for generative LLMs, and where encoder-decoder still shines.

item.title: A Close Reading of ‘Attention Is All You Need’
item.description: The original 2017 paper section by section, connecting each design choice to what you already know, and noting which ideas survived and which were replaced.

item.title: Mixture-of-Experts Layers
item.description: How MoE replaces the dense FFN with sparse expert routing, the load-balancing problem, and how expert-choice routing solves it.

item.title: Training View vs. Inference View
item.category: Arc 5: Decoding & the Real Inference Algorithm
item.description: Why the model you trained on full sequences behaves completely differently when it generates one token at a time, and what that means for everything that follows.

item.title: Prefill vs. Decode: The Two Phases of Inference
item.category: Arc 5: Decoding & the Real Inference Algorithm
item.description: How the prompt is processed in parallel (prefill) but generation is strictly sequential (decode), and why this split dominates every performance conversation.

item.title: Why One New Token Means One New Row
item.category: Arc 5: Decoding & the Real Inference Algorithm
item.description: Walking through the exact matrix operations at each decode step to see why generation is memory-bound, not compute-bound.

item.title: The KV Cache from First Principles
item.category: Arc 5: Decoding & the Real Inference Algorithm
item.description: Deriving the key-value cache by noticing which attention computations are redundant, then watching memory grow linearly with sequence length.

item.title: Sampling Strategies: Temperature, Top-k, Top-p, and Min-p
item.category: Arc 5: Decoding & the Real Inference Algorithm
item.description: How each strategy reshapes the probability distribution over the vocabulary, when to combine them, and what 'good randomness' actually looks like.

item.title: Speculative Decoding
item.category: Arc 5: Decoding & the Real Inference Algorithm
item.description: Using a small draft model to guess multiple tokens at once and a large model to verify them in parallel, turning sequential generation into a bet on acceptance rates.

item.title: Continuous Batching
item.category: Arc 5: Decoding & the Real Inference Algorithm
item.description: Why naive batching wastes GPU cycles on padding, and how iteration-level scheduling lets new requests join a running batch the moment a slot opens.

item.title: Prefix Caching and Prompt Reuse
item.category: Arc 5: Decoding & the Real Inference Algorithm
item.description: Sharing KV cache across requests that start with the same system prompt, and the cache-eviction policies that make it practical.

item.title: Structured and Constrained Generation
item.category: Arc 5: Decoding & the Real Inference Algorithm
item.description: How grammar-guided decoding and JSON-mode work by masking logits at each step, and the tradeoff between constraint strength and generation speed.

item.title: What an Inference Engine Actually Does
item.description: The concrete responsibilities — graph optimization, memory allocation, scheduling, kernel dispatch — that sit between your model weights and an HTTP response.

item.title: Kernel Fusion and the Memory Wall
item.description: Why fusing multiple operations into a single GPU kernel reduces memory round-trips, and how FlashAttention is the poster child for this idea.

item.title: PagedAttention: Virtual Memory for the KV Cache
item.description: Treating KV cache like virtual memory pages so you stop wasting 60-80% of GPU RAM on fragmentation.

item.title: Memory Management: Fitting a Model and Deciding Concurrency
item.description: A unified picture of where bytes go — weights, activations, KV cache, CUDA context — and how to reason about what fits on your GPU.

item.title: Quantization: INT8, INT4, GPTQ, AWQ, and GGUF
item.description: Shrinking weight precision to serve larger models on smaller hardware, with an honest look at what quality you lose and when.

item.title: Tensor, Pipeline, and Expert Parallelism
item.description: Three ways to split a model across multiple GPUs, each with different latency and throughput profiles.

item.title: Throughput vs. Latency: Picking Your Tradeoff
item.description: Why optimizing for tokens-per-second and optimizing for time-to-first-token are fundamentally in tension, and how batching policy mediates.

item.title: Comparing Engines: vLLM, TGI, TensorRT-LLM, llama.cpp, SGLang
item.description: A framework for choosing an inference stack based on your actual constraints — hardware, model size, latency budget, and deployment environment.

item.title: Benchmarking Your Own Inference Stack
item.description: How to run meaningful load tests, what metrics to capture, and why published benchmark numbers rarely transfer to your workload.

item.title: Pretraining Data: Mixtures, Curation, and What the Model Sees
item.description: How the composition and quality of the training corpus shapes capabilities more than architecture changes do.

item.title: Distributed Training: FSDP, DeepSpeed, and Megatron
item.description: The three dominant frameworks for spreading a training run across hundreds of GPUs, and the communication costs each one pays.

item.title: Supervised Fine-Tuning
item.description: Taking a pretrained base model and teaching it to follow instructions by training on (prompt, response) pairs, plus the formatting details that matter more than you'd think.

item.title: The RLHF Pipeline: Reward Models and PPO
item.description: How human preferences get compressed into a reward model, then used to steer generation via reinforcement learning, step by step.

item.title: DPO and Its Variants: Skipping the Reward Model
item.description: Why Direct Preference Optimization collapses the RLHF pipeline into a single supervised loss, and how IPO, KTO, and ORPO each tweak the formula.

item.title: Constitutional AI and RLAIF
item.description: Replacing human labelers with model-generated critiques guided by explicit principles, and what that buys you at scale.

item.title: Tool-Use Fine-Tuning
item.description: How models learn to emit structured tool calls, the data formats that work, and why function-calling reliability is a training problem, not a prompting problem.

item.title: Long-Context Training Techniques
item.description: RoPE scaling, progressive context extension, and the data strategies needed to make a model actually use its full context window.

item.title: Synthetic Data and Distillation
item.description: Using a stronger model to generate training data for a weaker one, when this works surprisingly well, and when it collapses.

item.title: LoRA and Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning
item.description: Freezing most weights and training low-rank adapters instead, with a clear picture of when PEFT matches full fine-tuning and when it falls short.

item.title: Loss vs. Benchmarks: Two Languages for Model Quality
item.description: Why validation loss is a smooth, reliable signal and benchmarks are noisy and gameable, but closer to what users actually care about.

item.title: Eval Harnesses: lm-eval-harness and HELM
item.description: How standardized evaluation frameworks work under the hood — prompt formatting, few-shot setup, metric aggregation — and why details matter enormously.

item.title: Contamination and Leakage
item.description: How benchmark answers end up in training data, the detection methods that exist, and why this problem is getting worse, not better.

item.title: Evaluating Reasoning
item.description: Why multiple-choice accuracy on MMLU tells you almost nothing about reasoning, and what newer evals like GPQA and FrontierMath attempt to measure instead.

item.title: Tool and Agent Evaluation
item.description: The unique challenges of evaluating multi-step tool use — partial credit, trajectory scoring, environment determinism — and why end-to-end pass rates hide most of the signal.

item.title: Human Preference Evaluation
item.description: How Chatbot Arena's Elo system works, what inter-annotator agreement looks like in practice, and the biases that style introduces over substance.

item.title: Calibration and Abstention
item.description: Whether a model's stated confidence matches its actual accuracy, and why teaching models to say 'I don't know' is an unsolved evaluation problem.

item.title: Embeddings from Scratch: From Word2Vec to E5
item.description: How text becomes geometry, from count-based vectors through contrastive learning to modern embedding models.

item.title: Vector Search and Approximate Nearest Neighbors
item.description: How HNSW, IVF, and product quantization make billion-scale similarity search practical in databases like Pinecone, Qdrant, and pgvector.

item.title: Dense, Sparse, and Hybrid Retrieval
item.description: Comparing BM25, learned-sparse models like SPLADE, dense embeddings, and the hybrid fusion strategies that outperform any single approach.

item.title: Chunking Strategies
item.description: Fixed-size, semantic, recursive, and parent-document chunking, and how chunk design dominates retrieval quality more than your embedding model does.

item.title: Rerankers and Cross-Encoders
item.description: Why a cheap first-stage retriever plus an expensive cross-encoder reranker beats a single-stage system, and how ColBERT bridges the gap.

item.title: RAG Architectures End to End
item.description: Tracing a query from ingestion through retrieval, reranking, prompt assembly, and generation — covering naive RAG, multi-hop, and agentic RAG patterns.

item.title: GraphRAG and Knowledge Graphs
item.description: How entity-relationship graphs enable multi-hop reasoning that flat vector search cannot, from Microsoft's GraphRAG to community-based summarization.

item.title: Context Windows: Advertised vs. Effective
item.description: Why a 1M-token window does not mean 1M tokens of useful recall, covering lost-in-the-middle effects, context rot, and working-memory bottlenecks.

item.title: Context Engineering: Compaction, Clearing, and Memory
item.description: Treating context as a scarce resource: sliding-window summarization, tool-result clearing, scratchpads, and sub-agent context isolation.

item.title: A Short History of Agents: From ReAct to 2026
item.description: The lineage from chain-of-thought prompting and ReAct through Toolformer, function calling, and today's production agent systems.

item.title: Function Calling as Structured Generation
item.description: How providers constrain decoder output to valid JSON tool calls using grammars, guided decoding, and schema-conditioned sampling.

item.title: The Agent Loop: Model, Runtime, Tool, Resume
item.description: Dissecting the core execute-observe-decide cycle that every agent framework implements, including error handling and retry logic.

item.title: Transcript Formats: How Providers Represent Tool Use
item.description: Comparing Anthropic's content-block array, OpenAI's tool_calls messages, and Gemini's function-call parts to understand what the model actually sees.

item.title: MCP: A Cross-System Standard for Tool Integration
item.description: What the Model Context Protocol solves, how servers expose tools/resources/prompts, and why it became the dominant standard for tool integration.

item.title: Remote MCP, OAuth, and Enterprise Auth
item.description: Moving MCP beyond local stdio: streamable HTTP transport, OAuth 2.1 with PKCE, and the enterprise authentication landscape.

item.title: Planning and Reasoning in Agents
item.description: How extended thinking, chain-of-thought budgets, and explicit planning steps improve agent task-success rates, and where they still fail.

item.title: Computer Use and Browser Agents
item.description: How screenshot-driven computer use and browser agents work, from Anthropic's approach to CUA, and their current safety boundaries.

item.title: Multi-Agent Systems and Agent-to-Agent Protocols
item.description: Orchestration patterns (supervisor, swarm, pipeline), Google's A2A protocol, and when multi-agent actually beats single-agent.
